The Dashboard is your financial command center -- a single-page overview of your accounts, spending, income, net worth, and upcoming bills.
When you log in, the Dashboard is the first page you see. It provides a comprehensive snapshot of your financial health using interactive charts and summary widgets.

Click Customize in the top-right of the dashboard header to tailor which widgets appear and in what order: Show or hide widgets -- remove any widget you don't want, or add one back later Reorder widgets -- drag a widget tile to a new position, or use the up/down arrow buttons (the arrow buttons also work on mobile, where widgets stack in a single column) Add opt-in widgets -- hidden widgets appear in a Hidden widgets tray beneath the layout; click one to add it to your dashboard Reset to default -- restore the standard layout at any time Your layout is saved to your account, so it syncs across all your devices .

Configurable widgets show a gear icon in their header. Click it to open that widget's settings, where (depending on the widget) you can: Choose a timeframe preset -- 1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, 2Y, 5Y, YTD, or All Filter the widget to specific accounts Toggle the chart type or view (for example, pie vs bar, or region vs country) Set a custom display name and description so the widget's header reads however you like These per-widget settings also persist across your devices.

The widgets below are hidden by default and can be added from the Customize dialog. Each is derived from a report, and most carry their own gear settings. Widget Shows Availability Favourite Reports The reports you've starred; click one to open it Always Portfolio Value Your total investment value over time Investments only Spending by Payee Spending grouped by payee Always Monthly Spending Trend Spending (and income) trended by month Always Income by Source Income grouped by source, as a pie or bar chart Always Credit Utilization by Account Utilization for each credit account Always Total Credit Utilization Combined used vs available credit Always Sector Allocation Portfolio breakdown by sector Investments only Security Type Allocation Holdings by security type (stocks, ETFs, and so on) Investments only Geographic Allocation Holdings by region, exchange, or country Investments only Top Recurring Expenses Your most frequent recurring expenses Always Weekend vs Weekday Spending Spending split between weekends and weekdays Always Note: The investment-related widgets (Portfolio Value, Sector Allocation, Security Type Allocation, and Geographic Allocation) only appear as options when you have investment holdings. Delegates: If you're viewing an account you've been granted access to, the dashboard is limited to the Favourite Accounts widget (plus Upcoming Bills, if that access was granted). The Customize button is hidden for delegates.

The top section of the dashboard displays your favourite accounts as summary cards. Each card shows: Account name and type Current balance in the account's currency Quick access to account transactions To mark an account as a favourite, go to Accounts and toggle the star icon on any account.

You can reorder your favourite account cards to arrange them in the order you prefer: On the Dashboard, click the Reorder button next to the favourite accounts section Drag and drop the account cards into your preferred order The new order is saved automatically

When a brokerage (investment) account is marked as a favourite, the dashboard card displays the account's market value rather than the cash balance. Clicking a brokerage favourite navigates to the Investments page filtered to that account.

This widget shows your scheduled bills and deposits that are coming due, ordered by date. Each entry shows: Payee name or transaction description Due date and how many days until due Amount of the scheduled transaction Account the transaction will be posted to This helps you anticipate upcoming cash flow needs and ensure sufficient funds are available.

If you have an active budget, the Budget Status widget provides a quick summary of your current budget period: Top 3 categories closest to their budget limits, with progress bars Safe to spend today -- How much you can spend per day and stay on track Days remaining in the current budget period Click the widget to navigate to the full Budget Dashboard . Note: This widget only appears if you have an active budget.

The Spending Insights widget surfaces automatically generated observations about your finances -- notable changes in spending, recurring patterns, and other things worth your attention. Each insight is a short, plain-language note derived from your recent activity. Click View all insights to open the full Insights page, where you can generate and review deeper analysis.

For new users, a Getting Started widget provides guidance on initial setup tasks: Creating accounts Adding transactions Setting up scheduled bills Importing data This widget disappears once you have completed the basic setup steps.

If you have investment accounts, the Top Movers widget shows the securities in your portfolio with the largest daily price changes (both gains and losses). This gives you a quick view of which investments are moving the most. Note: This widget only appears if you have at least one investment account with holdings.

The Favourite Securities widget lists the securities you've starred, each with its live quote and daily price change. It's a watchlist for the tickers you care about, whether or not you currently hold them. To add a security here, visit the Securities page and star the securities you want to track. Prices can be refreshed with the widget's refresh button. Note: This widget only appears once you have at least one security to track.

A pie chart breaks down your spending by category over a selectable timeframe (default: last month), optionally filtered to specific accounts. This provides an instant visual of where your money is going. Hover over a segment to see the category name and amount Categories are colour-coded for easy identification The chart includes expense categories only (income is excluded)

This bar chart compares your income and expenses over a selectable timeframe, optionally filtered by account. Each period shows: A green bar for total income A red bar for total expenses The visual difference helps you see periods where you spent more than you earned Income and expenses are classified by category type (income category vs expense category), not by the sign of the amount. Clicking on an income or expense bar navigates to the Transactions page filtered to the corresponding category type for that period.

The Net Worth chart tracks your total net worth over time, calculated monthly. It shows: Total assets (all positive-balance accounts plus investment market values) Total liabilities (credit cards, loans, mortgages, lines of credit) Net worth (assets minus liabilities) The chart provides a clear trend line showing whether your financial position is improving over time.

The Assets vs Liabilities widget presents a bar chart comparing your total assets against your total liabilities over time. Where the Net Worth chart tracks the single net figure, this widget shows the two sides side by side so you can see how each is trending on its own. Each period shows a bar for assets and a bar for liabilities The gap between the two bars reflects your net worth for that period
Investment prices and exchange rates can be refreshed manually from the dashboard using the refresh button. Prices are also updated automatically on weekdays at 5 PM EST.
Monize supports a wide variety of account types to represent your complete financial picture. This page covers creating, managing, and organizing your accounts.

Monize supports 10 account types: Account Type Description Typical Use Chequing Checking or current account Day-to-day banking Savings Savings account Emergency fund, short-term savings Credit Card Credit card account Credit card spending and payments Loan Installment loan Personal loans, auto loans Mortgage Mortgage account Home mortgage tracking Investment Brokerage account Stocks, ETFs, mutual funds Cash Cash wallet or petty cash Physical cash tracking Line of Credit Line of credit Revolving credit facilities Asset Asset tracking Property, vehicles, collectibles Other Miscellaneous Any account that does not fit other types

Credit Card accounts include a credit limit field. The available credit is calculated as credit limit - current balance . Loan, Mortgage, and Line of Credit accounts are debt accounts. They support interest rate tracking and a dedicated payment setup, and clicking them opens a per-account detail page rather than the transaction register. Loans and mortgages show an amortization schedule and payoff projection; lines of credit show a revolving-balance view. Mortgage accounts add Canadian-specific amortization settings. See Loan and Mortgage Setup . Investment accounts are always created as a linked pair -- a brokerage account (for holding securities) and a cash account (for the cash balance within the brokerage). See Investment Account Pairs for details. Asset accounts are used to track the value of physical assets like property or vehicles. Transactions on asset accounts represent changes in value.
Navigate to Accounts from the top navigation bar Click the Create Account button Fill in the account form:
Field Description Account Name A descriptive name for the account Account Type Select from the available types Currency The currency this account operates in

Field Description Opening Balance The starting balance (defaults to 0) Opening Date The date of the opening balance Institution The financial institution that holds the account (see Financial Institutions ). Optional for most account types, but required for loans and mortgages Account Number The institution's account number for your reference Credit Limit For credit cards only Interest Rate For savings, loans, and mortgages Notes Any additional notes about the account Click Save to create the account Tip: When importing from Microsoft Money, you do not need to create accounts manually if you plan to create them during the import process. However, creating accounts first gives you more control over the exact names, types, and opening balances. Note: When you choose a Loan or Mortgage account type, the form reveals extra payment fields. See Loan and Mortgage Setup below.

Selecting the Loan or Mortgage account type on the account form reveals a dedicated payment setup panel so Monize can track your amortization, split each payment into principal and interest, and project your payoff.

For a Loan (or line of credit), the following fields become available in addition to the standard fields: Field Description Payment Amount The regular payment made against the loan Payment Frequency Weekly, bi-weekly, monthly, quarterly, or yearly First Payment Date The date the first scheduled payment is due Payment-From Account The account the payment is drawn from (e.g. your chequing account) Interest Category The expense category the interest portion of each payment is booked to As you fill in the loan amount, interest rate, payment, frequency, and first payment date, a live amortization preview appears showing the principal and interest portions of the first payment, the total number of payments, and the estimated payoff date.

Mortgage accounts offer everything a loan does, plus mortgage-specific settings: Field Description Canadian mortgage Toggle for Canadian semi-annual interest compounding Variable rate Toggle to mark the mortgage as variable-rate Term Length The mortgage term, entered as years plus months Amortization Period The full amortization, entered as years plus months Payment Frequency Monthly, semi-monthly, bi-weekly, accelerated bi-weekly, weekly, or accelerated weekly First Payment Date , Payment-From Account , Interest Category Same as for loans The mortgage amortization preview shows the calculated payment amount, the effective annual rate , the first payment's principal and interest split, the total number of payments, total interest, and the estimated payoff date.

If you have already imported transaction history for a loan or mortgage, Monize can set up the payment for you. The guided payment setup analyses your existing transactions and detects: The payment cadence (frequency) and regular payment amount The principal / interest split from your most recent payment Any recurring extra principal payments An estimated interest rate, interest category, and source account Each detected value is presented with a confidence indicator (High, Medium, or Low) for you to review, adjust, and confirm before the payment schedule is created. You can also opt to auto-post future payments. If you are not sure how to record loan payments in the first place, a collapsible "How to record loan payments" guide is built into the form.

So that extra principal payments are scored correctly in the schedule, simulator, and Past Impact analysis, the account edit form lets you tell Monize how you record them. An overpayment is recognized as 100% principal when it matches any one of: A designated category A designated payee Memo text you specify Any single match is enough -- you do not have to use all three. The settings live in a gear menu on the account's edit form.

Banks book interest in different ways, and Monize reads all of them. An Interest booking mode setting (Auto / Split / Separate) tells Monize how to find the interest portion of each payment: Mode Use when Auto Let Monize detect the style automatically (the default) Split Each payment is a split transaction with a principal line and an interest line Separate Interest is booked as its own standalone expense transaction, apart from the principal transfer Interest-only grace periods appear as their own rows in the schedule. Interest is counted by its category across your full history regardless of the loan's configured start date, so a migrated loan's earlier activity is not hidden. If you refinance sequentially, give each refinance its own interest category so the periods stay cleanly separated. See the loan detail page tools for how recognized overpayments and interest flow into the simulator and rate detection.

Each account can record the financial institution that holds it -- the bank, brokerage, credit union, or lender behind the account. This is a free-text field on the account form, so you can enter the institution's name exactly as you want it to appear (for example, the name of your bank or your loan provider).

Identify accounts at a glance -- When you have several accounts of the same type, the institution name makes it clear which is which. Group related accounts -- Knowing the institution behind each account helps you see your overall exposure to any one bank or lender. Required for debt accounts -- The institution is mandatory for loan and mortgage accounts, since it identifies your lender. For all other account types it is optional.

Open the account form when creating a new account, or click the edit button on an existing account. Enter the institution name in the Institution field (up to 100 characters). Click Save . You can change an account's institution at any time by editing the account. The field is purely descriptive -- Monize does not connect to the institution, fetch logos, or detect the institution automatically; it is the name you type for your own reference.

The Accounts page displays all your accounts organized by type. Each account entry shows: Account name Account type indicator Current balance in the account's currency Currency code (if different from your home currency) Actions -- View transactions, Loan Details, Edit, Reconcile, Close (or Reopen), and Delete The available actions depend on the account: Loan Details appears only for loan, mortgage, and line-of-credit accounts and opens the account's detail page . Delete is only available for accounts with no transactions (see Deleting Accounts ), and closed accounts show Reopen in place of Close .
At the top of the accounts page, a summary card shows: Total assets -- Sum of all positive-balance accounts Total liabilities -- Sum of all debt accounts Net worth -- Assets minus liabilities

The filter bar above the list lets you narrow down which accounts are shown: Status -- A segmented control to switch between All , Active (currently in use), and Closed (closed/archived) accounts. Account type -- A dropdown to show only selected account types (e.g. only chequing and savings). It lists just the types you actually have; leaving it empty shows all types. Search -- A text box that filters accounts by name as you type. Click the X inside the box to clear the search. A counter beside the filters shows how many accounts match, in the form "X of Y accounts" . When the filters match nothing, a Clear Filters action resets the status, type, and search filters at once. Note: Your filter, sort, and density choices are remembered between visits.

Clicking into an account opens a detail page tailored to that account's type, rather than a plain transaction list. Each type surfaces the views that matter for it; a View Transactions button on every detail page takes you to the underlying register.

Balance history chart, with a 90-day balance forecast projected from your scheduled bills and deposits Recurring charges the account detects, each with one-click conversion to a scheduled bill A cash-flow mini-report for the account Top spending categories and payees , defaulting to a "This month" timeframe

Statement-cycle information and the current amount owed Spending breakdown by category for the cycle, including late-posting, unreconciled charges carried over from the previous cycle , so the amount owed is right Interest and fees tracking A payoff calculator and a 90-day projection A payment dialog for recording a card payment

Current value and purchase value , with appreciation metrics A quick value-update dialog to record a new valuation An equity panel when the asset is linked to its financing loan (for example, a house linked to its mortgage), showing value minus outstanding debt
Brokerage accounts open the Investments view for that account -- portfolio summary, asset allocation, value chart, holdings, and income tracking.

Loan, mortgage, and line-of-credit accounts open a per-account detail page at /accounts/[id] instead of the transaction register. You reach it by clicking a debt account in the list, or via the Loan Details row action . A View Transactions button on the page takes you to the underlying register.

For loans and mortgages, the top of the page shows a row of summary cards: Card Meaning Current Balance The amount still owed Original Amount The opening balance (or the amount derived from history) Interest Rate The annual rate; Canadian fixed mortgages also show the effective rate Payment The regular payment amount and its frequency Estimated Payoff Date When the loan is projected to be fully repaid Estimated Remaining Interest The interest still to be paid over the remaining schedule Below the cards, the page includes a month-grouped Loan Schedule with real per-row interest, an interactive Overpayment Simulator with saved what-if scenarios, an Impact of Overpayments Made (Past Impact) analysis, and an editable Rate History timeline. The schedule, rate history, and scenario comparison export to CSV , and the payoff comparison chart exports to PNG . See Loan Detail Page Tools for the full breakdown of each tool.

Because a line of credit revolves rather than amortizing to a fixed payoff, its detail page shows a revolving-balance view instead of an amortization schedule: Current Balance -- The amount currently drawn Credit Limit and Available Credit -- Shown when a credit limit is set Utilization % -- The portion of the limit in use, colour-coded to flag high utilization Peak Balance -- The highest balance reached (shown when no limit is set) Balance History -- A chart of the balance over time, counting both draws and repayments
Click the edit button on any account to modify its details. All fields from account creation can be updated.

When an account is no longer active (e.g., you closed a bank account), you can close it in Monize: Click the edit button on the account Toggle the Closed switch Click Save Closed accounts are hidden from the active accounts view and from transaction dropdowns, but their historical data is preserved for reporting.
Accounts can only be deleted if they have no transactions. If an account has transactions, you must either delete the transactions first or close the account instead.
Reconciliation helps you verify that your Monize records match your bank statement.

Navigate to the account you want to reconcile Click Reconcile Enter the statement ending balance and statement date from your bank Review each transaction: Cleared transactions match your bank statement Unreconciled transactions have not yet appeared on a statement Mark transactions as cleared by clicking on them When the difference is zero, click Finish Reconciling
Status Meaning Unreconciled New transaction, not yet on a statement Cleared Matches a bank statement entry Reconciled Previously cleared and locked Void Cancelled transaction

Mark accounts as favourites to have them displayed on the Dashboard: In the account list, click the star icon next to an account The account will appear in the Favourite Accounts widget on the Dashboard

When you create an Investment type account, Monize automatically creates two linked accounts: Brokerage Account -- Holds your securities (stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, etc.) Cash Account -- Tracks the cash balance within the brokerage These are linked internally. When you buy securities, the cash balance decreases. When you sell or receive dividends, the cash balance increases. The cash account is hidden from the main account list but is accessible through the investment interface. Clicking on a brokerage account in the account list navigates to the Investments page filtered to that account's holdings. For more details, see Investments . Important for Microsoft Money users: In Microsoft Money, investment accounts contain both securities and cash in a single account. In Monize, these are split into two linked accounts. When importing, the QIF parser handles this automatically -- the "Investment" export maps to the brokerage account and the "Regular" export maps to the cash account.

Each account has a designated currency. If you have accounts in different currencies: Transactions in that account are recorded in the account's currency The Dashboard and reports convert balances to your home currency using the latest exchange rates Cross-currency transfers record both amounts and the effective exchange rate For more details, see Currency Management .
Transactions are the core of your financial data in Monize. This page covers creating, searching, filtering, and managing transactions.
The Transactions page provides a comprehensive view of all your financial transactions across all accounts. It supports advanced filtering, search, and density controls for efficient data management.
Navigate to Transactions Click Add Transaction (or use the quick-add button) Fill in the transaction form:

Field Required Description Date Yes The date of the transaction Account Yes Which account this transaction belongs to Payee No Who the transaction was with Amount Yes The transaction amount (negative for expenses, positive for income) Category No The expense or income category Memo No Additional notes or description Tags No One or more tags for flexible labelling Reference No Cheque number or reference code Status No Unreconciled, Cleared, or Reconciled

The date field supports keyboard shortcuts for quick date entry: Key Action T Jump to today Y Jump to first day of the year R Jump to last day of the year M Jump to first day of the month H Jump to last day of the month + or = Next day - Previous day Page Up Next month Page Down Previous month Tip: On desktop, hover over the info icon next to the date label to see these shortcuts. The calendar popover also has a year picker , so you can jump to a distant year in one step instead of paging month by month.
If the payee does not exist, you can create a new one directly from the transaction form without leaving the page.

The transaction form includes a history button (clock icon) next to the Payee field. Clicking it opens a popover listing recent transactions, and selecting one quick-fills the form with the payee, category, amount, memo, and tags from that transaction. You can then adjust any field before saving. The history button appears on the new transaction form only -- it is hidden when editing an existing transaction. It is also available in split mode : selecting a recent split entry copies its payee and rebuilds the split rows from the source transaction. The popover behaves differently depending on whether a payee is selected: Context What the popover shows No payee selected A globally deduped list of your recent transactions, with one row per unique payee/category combination. Useful when you have not decided what you are entering yet. Payee selected (or typed) The most recent transactions for that specific payee, in raw chronological order with no dedup. Useful for repeating a familiar purchase exactly. For payee-scoped results, free-text payee names are matched exactly. If you have not selected an existing payee from the dropdown but have typed a name that matches a previous free-text entry, the popover scopes to that name. Splits are included. A split parent appears as a single row labelled "Split: Category A, Category B" (truncated with a count if more than two categories). Selecting it rebuilds the full split breakdown in the form. Transfers are excluded. Transfers between accounts are managed through their own form mode and do not appear in the quick-fill list. The number of entries shown in the popover is configurable from 3 to 20 (default 5 ). Adjust it under Settings -> Preferences -> Transactions -> Recent transactions in quick-fill . See Settings and Security for details. Tip: When you are creating a transaction for a payee you visit often, type or pick the payee first, then open the history -- you will see only that payee's prior entries in date order, which is faster than scrolling the global list.

The transaction list displays your transactions in a table with the following columns: Column Description Date Transaction date Account Account name Payee Who the transaction was with Category Assigned category (or "Split" if multiple categories) Memo Transaction notes Amount Transaction amount (red for expenses, green for income) Balance Running balance for the account Status Reconciliation status indicator

You can adjust the display density to fit more or fewer transactions on screen: Normal -- Default spacing with generous padding Compact -- Reduced padding, fits more transactions on screen Dense -- Minimal padding for maximum data density
Transactions are paginated at 50 per page. Use the pagination controls at the bottom of the list to navigate between pages.
The filter panel provides powerful options for finding specific transactions.

Filter Description Accounts Filter by one or more accounts Account Status Show active or archived accounts Categories Filter by one or more categories Payees Filter by one or more payees Tags Filter by one or more tags Date Range Set start and end dates Amount Range Set a minimum and/or maximum amount (min/max) Status Filter by one or more reconciliation statuses (Unreconciled, Cleared, Reconciled, Void) Time Period Quick presets that set the date range for you: Today, Yesterday, This Week, Last Week, Month to Date, Last Month, Year to Date, Last Year, Last 30 Days, Last 365 Days, All Dates, or Custom Search Free-text search across payee, memo, reference, and category and tag names. If what you type parses as an amount in your number format (respecting your decimal and grouping separators) it also matches transactions with that exact amount, and if it parses as a date in your date format (ISO YYYY-MM-DD is always accepted) it matches transactions on that exact date Note: When the filter panel is collapsed, each active filter appears as a removable chip -- click the x on a chip to clear just that filter. If any of your accounts are marked as favourites, a Favourites row of quick-select buttons appears above the panel so you can limit the list to a favourite account in one tap.

When you filter the list to a single payee or a single category , an info widget appears alongside the transactions summarizing that payee or category -- the same way the account widget summarizes a single-account view. It gives you an at-a-glance total and context for what you are looking at without leaving the page.

Your filter selections are saved in your browser's local storage, so they persist between sessions. When navigating from a report, the report's filters are applied via URL parameters and override your saved filters temporarily.
Above the list, two charts summarize the transactions currently in view. Both follow your active filters and timeframe.

A time-aware bar chart of income and expense totals. It rolls up to an adaptive Month / Quarter / Year granularity (auto-selected by the span in view, with a manual toggle) and gap-fills empty periods , so bars are spaced by real elapsed time rather than one equal-width bar per active period. The axis and tooltip are labelled by period, you can drill down into a bucket , and averages are computed over elapsed periods.

A running-balance chart for the account(s) in view. When no start-date filter is set, it can span your account's entire history (an all-time mode), kept fast by server-side downsampling to at most 400 points while always keeping the latest; the axis switches between month and year labels as the span grows, and an all-zero (e.g. closed) account shows a banner. For liability accounts (credit cards, loans, mortgages, lines of credit) a negative balance is normal, so the chart uses a neutral Min Balance label instead of flagging the low point as a warning.
A split transaction distributes a single payment across multiple categories. For example, a supermarket purchase might be split between "Groceries" and "Household Supplies."

In the transaction form, click Split Add multiple category/amount rows Each row has its own category, amount, optional memo, and optional tags The split amounts must total the transaction amount Click Save Split transactions display "Split" in the category column of the transaction list. Click on the transaction to see the full breakdown.
Transfers move money between your accounts (e.g., from chequing to savings).

In the transaction form, select the source account Choose the Transfer to account (the destination) Enter the amount Optionally choose a category (see the note below) Click Save Monize creates two linked transactions -- one in each account. The source account shows a withdrawal and the destination shows a deposit. Note: A transfer is never counted as income or an expense. Assigning it a category is optional and does not change that -- but a categorised transfer does appear in the monthly category breakdown, which is handy for tracking things like recurring investment contributions.
If the source and destination accounts are in different currencies, you may need to adjust the exchange rate or amounts after import. See Currency Management for details.

Click on any transaction in the list to open it in the edit form. Modify any field and click Save . Note: Monize warns you before you edit or delete a reconciled transaction , so a carefully balanced statement does not drift by accident. You can still proceed after confirming.
Voiding a transaction reverses its effect on the account balance but preserves the record for audit purposes. The transaction amount is set to zero and the status changes to Void .

Deleting permanently removes a transaction. This action cannot be undone. The account balance is adjusted accordingly. Caution: If the transaction is part of a linked transfer, deleting it will also affect the linked transaction in the other account.
Bulk Update allows you to modify multiple transactions at once, such as changing the category, payee, or status for a batch of transactions.

Open the Filters panel on the Transactions page Click the Bulk Update button (located next to the "Show accounts" controls on desktop, or at the bottom of the filter panel on mobile) Checkboxes will appear next to each transaction in the list

Click the checkbox next to individual transactions to select them Use the select all checkbox in the table header to select all transactions on the current page If all transactions on the page are selected, a banner will offer to select all matching transactions across all pages (useful when filters are applied)

After selecting transactions, click Bulk Update in the selection banner In the Bulk Update dialog, choose which fields to update: Category -- Assign a new category to all selected transactions Payee -- Change the payee for all selected transactions Status -- Update the reconciliation status (Unreconciled, Cleared, Reconciled, or Void) Only fields you modify will be updated; other fields are left unchanged Click Apply to save the changes
Click Cancel Bulk in the filter panel to exit without making changes Completing a bulk update automatically exits bulk mode Clicking Clear selection in the selection banner also exits bulk mode
You can delete multiple transactions at once using the same selection mechanism as Bulk Update.

Enter bulk mode using the Bulk Update button in the filter panel Select transactions using checkboxes (individual, page-level, or all matching) Click Delete in the selection banner Confirm the deletion in the dialog
Mode Description By selection Deletes the specific transactions you selected by checkbox By filter Deletes all transactions matching the current filter criteria (when "select all matching" is used)

Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone Linked transfer counterparts are automatically deleted along with the selected transaction Account balances are recalculated after deletion A confirmation dialog shows the count of transactions to be deleted before proceeding

Each transaction has a reconciliation status: Status Icon Description Unreconciled (blank) New transaction, not yet verified against a statement Cleared C Verified to match a bank statement entry Reconciled R Locked as part of a completed reconciliation Void V Cancelled, zero-amount record preserved The status flow is typically: Unreconciled -> Cleared -> Reconciled You can change the status from the transaction list by clicking the status indicator, or during the account reconciliation process. See Account Reconciliation for details.
The Copy dropdown on each transaction row provides two actions:

Creates a copy of the transaction with the same account, payee, amount, category, tags, and memo. The duplicate opens in the transaction form so you can adjust any fields (such as the date) before saving.

Converts a transaction into a recurring scheduled transaction. The scheduled transaction form opens pre-filled with the transaction's details. Set the frequency, start date, and other scheduling options, then click Save . The original transaction is not modified in either case. For more on scheduled transactions, see Bills and Deposits .

Monize tracks your recent actions and lets you undo and redo them using keyboard shortcuts: Shortcut Action Ctrl+Z (or Cmd+Z on Mac) Undo the last action Ctrl+Shift+Z (or Cmd+Shift+Z on Mac) Redo the last undone action Ctrl+Y (or Cmd+Y on Mac) Redo (alternative shortcut) Undo and redo work across all data pages -- transactions, accounts, categories, payees, tags, securities, budgets, scheduled transactions, and custom reports. A toast notification confirms each undo or redo operation. Note: These shortcuts are disabled when focus is inside a text input field, so they do not interfere with normal text editing.

Monize includes a full-featured budget planner that analyzes your spending history to auto-generate realistic budgets, tracks spending in real-time with velocity projections, supports flexible rollover strategies per category, and proactively alerts you before you overspend.

Navigate to Budgets from the top navigation bar to view your active budget or create a new one. The budget system integrates with your transactions, scheduled bills, and categories to provide a complete picture of your financial plan.
Monize includes a Budget Wizard that analyzes your historical spending to suggest realistic targets -- no manual data entry required. The wizard walks you through four steps.

Choose a strategy -- Select one of four budget strategies (see Budget Strategies below). Each strategy is displayed as a card with a description. Select an analysis period -- Choose 3, 6, or 12 months of spending history to analyze. Longer periods smooth out anomalies; shorter periods reflect recent habits. Choose a profile -- Pick how aggressive your targets should be: Profile Description Comfortable Based on the 75th percentile of your spending -- allows headroom On Track Based on median spending -- a realistic, sustainable target Aggressive Based on the 25th percentile -- a stretch goal for maximum savings Click Analyze My Spending to generate suggestions. The analysis calculates statistical distributions per category, identifies fixed expenses (rent, subscriptions) vs variable spending (dining, groceries), and estimates your monthly income.

This step displays every spending category found in your history, grouped into: Income categories at the top Expense categories sorted by suggested amount (largest first) Transfer accounts (savings contributions, loan payments) For each category, you can see: Column Description Category The spending category name Avg/mo Your average monthly spending Suggested The wizard's recommended budget amount Amount Editable -- adjust to your preference Use the profile toggle buttons (Comfortable / On Track / Aggressive) at the top to quickly switch between suggested amounts for all categories at once. For 50/30/20 strategy budgets, categories are grouped into Needs, Wants, and Savings with percentage targets shown. You can also add categories that weren't found in your history, or remove categories you don't want to track.

Configure your budget settings: Setting Description Budget Name A descriptive name (defaults to current month + year) Budget Type Monthly, Annual, or Pay Period Start Date When the budget takes effect Rollover Default rollover strategy for all categories (None, Monthly, Quarterly, Annual) Alert Thresholds Warning percentage (default 80%) and critical percentage (default 95%) Income Linked Enable percentage-based budgeting tied to actual income Base Monthly Income Your expected monthly income (uses the standard currency input with symbol and formatting) Excluded Accounts Accounts to exclude from budget tracking (e.g., investment accounts)

The review step shows a complete summary of your budget before creation: Budget details -- Name, type, strategy, start date, rollover setting, alert thresholds Summary cards -- Estimated income, total expenses, transfers, and remaining balance Category table -- All categories with amounts and types (income, expense, transfer) On mobile, the Type column is hidden to provide more room for category names and amounts. Click Create Budget to finalize.
The budget dashboard ( /budgets/[id] ) is your primary view for tracking budget progress in real time.

Four cards at the top provide an at-a-glance overview: Card Description Total Budget Your total budgeted amount for the period, with category count Spent Total spending so far, with percentage of budget used Remaining Budget remaining, with days left in the period Savings Projected savings (income minus expenses)

A circular gauge (0--100) summarizing how well you're sticking to your budget. Score Range Label 90--100 Excellent 70--89 Good 50--69 Needs Attention Below 50 Off Track The score factors in: Categories over budget (deductions proportional to overage) Categories consistently under budget (bonus points) Essential categories weighted higher than discretionary Month-over-month improvement trends

Shows your spending pace and whether you'll finish the month within budget: Daily burn rate -- How much you're spending per day Safe to spend -- How much you can spend per day and stay on track Projected month-end -- Where you'll land at the current pace Pace indicator -- Green (under pace), yellow (near pace), red (over pace) The velocity widget also factors in upcoming bills from your scheduled transactions, so "safe to spend" reflects your truly available discretionary budget.

A sortable list of all budget categories with progress bars and real-time tracking. Each category row shows: Category name and group (if using 50/30/20) Progress bar -- Colour-coded by percentage used (green, yellow, red) with a pace marker showing where you should be today Amount spent vs budgeted amount and percentage Pace status -- Whether you're ahead of or behind the safe spending pace Use the Sort dropdown to sort by name, percentage used, amount spent, remaining amount, or pace status. On mobile, the sort controls stack below the heading for better readability.

If you've assigned categories to flex groups, the Flex Groups widget shows aggregate spending. Individual categories within a group can be over budget, but as long as the group total is within limits, no alert fires.

Integrates with your scheduled transactions to show: Bills coming due this period with dates and amounts Truly available budget -- remaining budget minus upcoming bills This prevents a false sense of security when you have budget left but bills pending
A calendar-style heatmap showing daily spending intensity. Darker cells indicate higher spending days, helping you identify patterns.
A line chart showing your budgeted amount vs actual spending over the past several months. Helps identify whether you're improving over time.

Monize supports four budget strategies, each suited to different financial styles: Strategy Description Fixed Set fixed amounts per category. Simple and predictable. Unused budget disappears at the end of each period. Rollover Unused budget carries forward to the next period based on per-category rollover rules. Good for saving toward irregular expenses. Zero-Based Every dollar of income must be assigned to a category. Income minus expenses equals zero. Forces intentional allocation of every dollar. 50/30/20 Categories are tagged as Needs (50%), Wants (30%), or Savings (20%). The wizard auto-calculates targets based on your income.

Each category can have its own rollover strategy: Rollover Type Description None Budget resets each period -- no carry-forward Monthly Unused budget rolls to the next month Quarterly Budget accumulates for 3 months then resets Annual Budget accumulates all year You can also set a rollover cap to limit how much accumulates. For example, a clothing category might roll over monthly with a $500 cap. Common patterns: Groceries -- None (no point accumulating) Clothing -- Monthly with a cap (save for seasonal shopping) Travel -- Annual (vacation fund) Car Maintenance -- Annual with no cap (save for repairs)

For freelancers, gig workers, or anyone with variable income, you can enable income-linked budgeting. When enabled, category budget amounts are treated as percentages of your actual income rather than fixed dollar amounts. If your income drops, your budget automatically tightens If your income rises, your budget grows proportionally The dashboard shows both the percentage and the resulting dollar amount Set a Base Monthly Income to establish the baseline. The budget wizard will suggest this based on your historical income data.
Monize proactively monitors your budget and sends alerts before you overspend.

Alert Type Trigger Severity Pace Warning Daily burn rate projects >110% of budget by period end Warning Threshold Warning Category spending reaches the warning threshold (default 80%) Warning Threshold Critical Category spending reaches the critical threshold (default 95%) Critical Over Budget Category spending exceeds 100% Critical Flex Group Warning Flex group total reaching 90% Warning Projected Overspend Current velocity projects >15% over budget Warning Income Shortfall Actual income below 80% of expected (income-linked budgets) Critical Positive Milestone 50%+ through the period and under 60% of budget Success Bill Due A manually-tracked bill is coming due soon Info

A bell icon in the top navigation bar shows the count of unread alerts. Click the bell to open the alert dropdown. The alert dropdown displays: Severity badges -- Colour-coded (red for critical, yellow for warning, green for good news, blue for info) Alert title and message -- What happened and the details Unread indicator -- A dot on unread alerts Mark All Read button -- Clears all unread indicators at once Dismiss button -- An X button on each alert to remove it (see below) Clicking an alert navigates to the relevant budget page. Bill due alerts navigate to the Bills & Deposits page instead.

Each alert in the dropdown has an X button that appears on hover. Clicking it: Immediately removes the alert from the list Shows a toast notification with an Undo button for 5 seconds If you don't undo, the alert is permanently deleted after 5 seconds If you click Undo , the alert is restored to the list Virtual bill due alerts (which are generated on-the-fly, not stored in the database) are removed from the list immediately but don't trigger a backend delete.

Budget alert emails can be enabled in Settings : Email Type Description Immediate alerts Sent for critical threshold, over-budget, and income shortfall alerts Weekly digest Summary of all alerts, health score, and safe daily spend (configurable for Monday or Friday) Monthly summary End-of-period report with total budget vs actual, savings achieved, and health score Configure email preferences in Settings > Notifications .

Budgets are divided into periods (typically monthly). At the end of each period: The current period is closed automatically (via a daily cron job on the 1st of each month) Actual spending is finalized Rollover amounts are calculated per category A new period is opened with rollover balances carried forward You can also manually close a period from the budget settings.

Use the Period Selector dropdown on the budget dashboard to switch between the current period and historical periods. Historical periods show: Final actual amounts per category Rollover in/out amounts Budget vs actual comparison

Nine budget-specific reports are available in the Reports section: Report Description Budget vs Actual Compare your budgeted amounts to actual spending over time across all categories Budget Health Score Get a 0--100 health score for your budget with detailed per-category impact analysis Seasonal Spending Patterns Discover seasonal trends and high-spending months across your budget categories Budget Trend Line chart showing total budgeted vs total actual spending over 6--12 months to track improvement Category Performance Table showing each category's budget performance over multiple months with trend indicators Savings Rate Track your savings rate (income minus expenses divided by income) over time vs your target Health Score History Line chart of monthly budget health scores showing your financial trajectory over time Flex Group Analysis Stacked bar chart for each flex group showing component categories with group limit reference Seasonal Spending Map Heatmap grid showing 12 months across all categories to identify seasonal spending patterns Additionally, a Budget Variance metric is available in the custom report builder, so you can create your own budget-related reports with flexible filters and groupings.

The Scenario Planner is a "what-if" tool for trying budget changes without committing them. Navigate to your budget dashboard Open the Scenario Planner Adjust category amounts using sliders See live projections: savings impact, flex group effects, zero-based balance changes Click Apply Changes to save your adjustments, or discard them This is entirely a frontend calculation -- no data is saved until you explicitly apply changes.

To edit an existing budget: Navigate to the budget dashboard Click Edit in the top right Modify budget settings (name, type, strategy, categories, amounts, rollover rules, alert thresholds) Click Save You can also: Add categories that weren't included in the original budget Remove categories you no longer want to track Bulk update all category amounts at once Change rollover rules per category
Monize provides comprehensive investment portfolio tracking with automatic price updates, cost basis calculation, and performance reporting.
The Investments page gives you a complete picture of your investment portfolio, including current market values, unrealized gains/losses, and daily price movements.

Investment accounts in Monize are composed of two linked accounts: Component Purpose Brokerage Account Holds your securities (stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, bonds) Cash Account Tracks the cash balance within the brokerage When you create an investment account, both components are created automatically. The cash account is hidden from the main Accounts list but is managed through the Investments interface.

Buying securities decreases the cash balance and adds to holdings Selling securities increases the cash balance and reduces holdings Dividends increase the cash balance Transfers move cash in or out of the investment account Microsoft Money users: In Microsoft Money, the cash and securities are combined in a single investment account. Monize separates these for cleaner transaction tracking, but the import process handles this mapping automatically.

The portfolio view shows all your investment holdings grouped by account. You can filter the view to a specific account using the account selector at the top of the page. Tip: You can navigate directly to the Investments page filtered by a specific account by clicking on a brokerage account from the Accounts page or from a brokerage favourite on the Dashboard .

At the top, a summary card shows: Total Market Value -- Current value of all investment holdings Total Cost Basis -- What you paid for all holdings Total Unrealized Gain/Loss -- The difference (both dollar and percentage) Cash Balances -- Total cash across all investment accounts

Each holding displays: Column Description Security Name and symbol of the security Quantity Number of shares/units held Average Cost Your average cost per share Current Price Latest market price Market Value Current total value (quantity x current price) Unrealized Gain/Loss Difference from cost basis (both $ and %) Holdings are colour-coded: green for gains, red for losses.

The Investments page includes an Asset Allocation donut chart with a grouping toggle: Grouping When available By security Always By tag Only when your holdings are tagged By key Only when your holdings carry key:value tags By country Only when country allocation data exists Each view shows the top 10 slices plus an Other band that groups the remaining smaller holdings. Allocation percentages always reconcile against the drawn slices, so the legend and the chart agree exactly. By key charts your portfolio's value-weighted split across the values of a chosen tag key (for example, splitting by a country or strategy key). By country performs a geographic look-through : rather than grouping by an ETF's listing exchange, it looks through your funds to their underlying holdings and reports true country-level exposure -- the top 10 countries individually, with the rest collapsed into an Other Countries band.
The page also shows a Portfolio Value Over Time chart with a range selector (1D, 1W, 1M, and longer ranges up to All). A View report link opens the full Portfolio Value report for a richer breakdown.

Monize supports 9 investment transaction types: Action Description Cash Impact Buy Purchase securities Cash decreases Sell Sell securities Cash increases Dividend Cash dividend received Cash increases Interest Interest income received Cash increases Capital Gain Realized or unrealized capital gains Cash increases Reinvest Dividend reinvested as additional shares No cash change Split Stock split adjustment No cash change Transfer In Securities moved in from another account No cash change Transfer Out Securities moved out to another account No cash change
Navigate to Investments Select the brokerage account Click Add Transaction Select the transaction type (Buy, Sell, Dividend, etc.) Fill in the details:

Field Description Date Transaction date Action Transaction type (Buy, Sell, etc.) Security The security involved Quantity Number of shares/units Price Price per share/unit Commission Any trading commission or fee Total Calculated total (quantity x price + commission) Description Optional notes
Securities represent the stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, bonds, and other instruments you trade.
Navigate to Tools > Securities to manage your security master list.

Field Description Symbol Ticker symbol (e.g., AAPL, VGRO.TO) Name Full name (e.g., Apple Inc.) Type STOCK, ETF, MUTUAL_FUND, BOND, GIC, CASH, or OTHER Exchange Stock exchange (NYSE, NASDAQ, TSX, etc.) Currency The currency the security trades in Description Free-text notes, auto-populated from the Yahoo provider profile during symbol lookup Tags User-assignable tags that drive the by-tag allocation view
Securities can be added: Manually from the Securities page During import (mapped or auto-created from QIF data) Automatically when creating investment transactions

Securities that are not used in any investment account can be deleted from the Securities page. Click the delete button next to a security to remove it. If the security is referenced by any holdings or investment transactions, it cannot be deleted until those references are removed.

When looking up securities, Monize searches Yahoo Finance and ranks results by exchange. If you primarily invest on non-US exchanges, you can set Preferred Exchanges in Settings to prioritize results from your exchanges. See Settings > Preferred Exchanges for details.
Security prices are updated automatically and can also be refreshed manually.
Schedule: Weekdays (Monday-Friday) at 5:00 PM EST Source: Yahoo Finance Data: Daily OHLCV (Open, High, Low, Close, Volume)
Click the Refresh Prices button on the Investments page or Dashboard to trigger an immediate price update.

You can add, edit, and delete individual price entries for any security. This is useful for: Securities not tracked by Yahoo Finance (e.g., private funds, GICs) Correcting incorrect price data Adding NAV prices for mutual funds To manage prices: Navigate to Tools > Securities Click on a security to view its price history Use the Add Price , Edit , or Delete buttons on individual entries Manual prices (source: "manual") take priority over Yahoo Finance prices for the same date. If you delete a manual price and investment transactions exist on that date, the system automatically backfills the price from the transaction's buy/sell price.

Monize can populate security prices from your investment transaction history. When you buy or sell a security at a specific price, that price can be used to fill gaps in the price history. This is especially useful for securities with skipPriceUpdates enabled or securities not available on Yahoo Finance. Transaction-based prices are automatically created during import. For existing data, you can trigger a manual backfill from the browser console (see Issues below).
When you import investment data or add a new security, Monize automatically backfills historical prices (up to 10 years). This ensures accurate portfolio valuation for historical reporting.
Monize tracks your cost basis using the average cost method .

When you buy shares, the total cost is added to your cost basis The average cost per share is: total cost basis / total shares held When you sell shares, the cost basis for the sold shares is calculated using the average cost Reinvested dividends add to both quantity and cost basis

When all shares of a security are sold, the holding is removed from your portfolio. If you buy the same security again, a new cost basis starts from that purchase.

Importing investment data from Microsoft Money requires special handling. See the Importing from Microsoft Money guide for complete details.

The recommended method is to import the .mny file directly. Investment accounts, securities, buys, sells, dividends, reinvestments, share transfers, stock splits and price history all come across in one pass, and share counts are reconciled against Money's own open tax lots afterwards If you use the older QIF method instead, Microsoft Money exports investment accounts as two separate QIF files: "Investment" type for securities transactions and "Regular" type for cash transactions Import the investment brokerage file first, then the cash file With QIF, securities must be mapped to existing records or created during import Monize automatically creates the linked cash transactions when importing investment QIF files For the recommended QIF import order, see Recommended Import Order .

The Bills & Deposits feature lets you schedule recurring transactions so you never miss a payment or forget about regular income.

Bills & Deposits manages your recurring financial obligations and expected income. It displays upcoming transactions, provides a cash flow forecast, and can automatically post transactions on their due dates.
Navigate to Bills & Deposits from the top navigation bar Click Add Scheduled Transaction Fill in the form:

Field Required Description Account Yes Which account this transaction uses Payee No Who the transaction is with Amount Yes Transaction amount Category No Expense or income category Frequency Yes How often the transaction recurs Start Date Yes When the recurring schedule begins End Date No When to stop recurring (optional) Total Occurrences No Maximum number of occurrences (alternative to end date) Tags No One or more tags applied when the transaction is posted Reminder Days No How many days before due date to show a reminder Auto-Post No Whether to automatically create the transaction on the due date Memo No Additional notes
Like regular transactions, scheduled transactions support splits across multiple categories. Turn on the Split this transaction toggle in the form to add multiple category/amount rows.

You can schedule recurring transfers between accounts (e.g., a monthly transfer from chequing to savings). Select a Transfer to account instead of a category. You may optionally also assign a category: the transfer is still not counted as income or expense, but it will appear in the monthly category breakdown (useful for tracking recurring investment contributions).

Frequency Description Once A single future transaction (useful for reminders) Daily Every day Weekly Once per week on a specific day Bi-Weekly Every two weeks Every 4 Weeks Every four weeks (useful for pay cycles that do not align to calendar months) Monthly Once per month on a specific date Quarterly Every three months Yearly Once per year

The Bills & Deposits page shows all scheduled transactions with: Column Description Description/Payee Who or what the transaction is for Account The account involved Amount The scheduled amount Frequency How often it recurs Next Due Date When the next occurrence is due Status Active, paused, or completed
When auto-posting is enabled for a scheduled transaction, Monize automatically creates the transaction on its due date without any manual intervention.

Each day, the system checks for scheduled transactions that are due If auto-post is enabled, the transaction is created in the designated account The next occurrence date is calculated based on the frequency If the total occurrences limit is reached, the scheduled transaction is marked as completed
Fixed-amount bills (e.g., rent, subscription services) -- The amount is the same each time Regular transfers (e.g., monthly savings contribution) -- Predictable, consistent amounts
Variable-amount bills (e.g., utilities, credit card payments) -- Use reminders instead and enter the actual amount manually
You can modify or skip individual occurrences of a scheduled transaction without changing the overall schedule.

In the bills list, find the scheduled transaction Click on the specific upcoming occurrence Change the date, amount, or category for this occurrence only To split just this occurrence across multiple categories, turn on the Split this occurrence toggle and add category/amount rows (independent of whether the underlying schedule is split) Click Save Override The override only affects that single occurrence. All other future occurrences follow the original schedule.
If a recurring bill does not apply for a particular period (e.g., a holiday causes a payment to be skipped): Select the occurrence Choose Skip this occurrence The next occurrence continues as normal

The bills system provides a cash flow forecast showing your expected account balances based on scheduled transactions. This helps you: Anticipate when account balances will be low Plan for upcoming large expenses Ensure sufficient funds for automatic payments
For loan and mortgage accounts, scheduled transactions can be set up to track regular payments.

Create a scheduled transaction with the loan payment amount Set the category to the loan account (this creates a transfer to the loan) Set the appropriate frequency (typically monthly) This ensures each payment is recorded as a transfer to the loan account, properly reducing the outstanding balance. Note: When importing from Microsoft Money, loan payment categories are automatically detected and mapped to the corresponding loan accounts. See Importing from Microsoft Money for details.

You can create a scheduled transaction from any existing transaction without re-entering its details. On the Transactions page, find the transaction you want to schedule Click the Copy dropdown on the transaction row and select Schedule as Recurring The scheduled transaction form opens pre-filled with the transaction's account, payee, amount, category, and tags Set the frequency, start date, and other scheduling options Click Save The original transaction is not modified -- a new scheduled transaction is created based on its details.

When email notifications are enabled in Settings , Monize sends reminder emails before scheduled transactions come due. Reminder emails are colour-coded to help you quickly distinguish between expenses and income at a glance.

Monize can read order confirmations from a mailbox and turn them into itemized transactions: it finds the bank transaction the email belongs to, fills in the line items, and shows you what it proposes before anything changes. This page covers connecting the mailbox -- a Gmail account above all, since Google's rules decide how you should connect, then Microsoft 365 and any other IMAP server -- and what to do when the connection fails. How emails are read, matched and approved (profiles, the Emails tab, AI assistance) is documented separately.

Where it lives. The Email Receipts hub is under Tools in the main menu (and as a card on the Settings page). It has four tabs: Overview , Emails , Profiles and Mailbox . The mailbox connection itself is at Settings > Email Receipts . What it reads. Order confirmations are read from a dedicated mailbox over IMAP. Monize only reads it: it never changes, moves or deletes a message, and it opens the folder read-only. How often. With Read the mailbox automatically on, the folder is read every 15 minutes. Poll now reads it on demand at any time. Use a dedicated mailbox. Every message in the folder is read, so it should hold nothing but order confirmations. With Gmail the natural "dedicated mailbox" is a label : create a filter that applies a label such as Receipts to the shops' confirmations, and point Monize at that label. Gmail labels appear to IMAP as folders (a nested label is written Parent/Child ). Who can use it. The account owner only. A delegate sees neither the settings nor the receipts pages. What it needs on the server. ENCRYPTION_KEY must be set: a mailbox password or sign-in is stored encrypted, and cannot be saved without it.

There are two ways to connect a Gmail mailbox, and Google's policies -- not Monize -- decide which one fits you. IMAP has no narrower Google scope than https://mail.google.com/ , which Google classes as restricted : an app that asks for it must either be verified by Google (an annual, paid security assessment) or live with the limits Google puts on unverified apps. Path What you need Limits Best for A. App password through the manual IMAP form A personal Google account with 2-Step Verification on Not available for Google Workspace ("work, school or organization") accounts, accounts in Advanced Protection, or accounts whose 2-Step Verification uses security keys only Personal Gmail. Start here. No Google Cloud project, nothing to verify, no expiry. B. Connect with Google , audience External , status Testing A Google Cloud project with an OAuth client (set up by the administrator) Only the test users listed on the project (up to 100) can connect, and every grant expires after 7 days -- the mailbox then stops and asks to be reconnected Trying the feature out, or a tiny group that accepts a weekly Reconnect C. Connect with Google , audience Internal A Google Workspace organisation, with the Cloud project inside it Only accounts in that Workspace domain can connect A family or business on Google Workspace. No verification, no 7-day expiry. D. Monize does not offer this. Both Google paths give Monize the same access: a scope that could write to the mailbox. Monize still opens the folder read-only and exposes no write operation, so the mailbox is never changed.
An app password is a 16-character passcode that lets one app sign in to your Google account without your real password. It is the simplest way to connect a personal Gmail account.

h: 1. Create the app password in Google
x: Turn on 2-Step Verification for the Google account if it is not already on (Google Account > Security). App passwords exist only on accounts with 2-Step Verification. Open myaccount.google.com/apppasswords , give the password a name such as Monize receipts and click Create . Copy the 16 characters shown. Google shows them once; spaces are ignored. Advanced Protection: app passwords are not available on an account enrolled in Google's Advanced Protection Program , and enrolling later revokes any app password already created, so a mailbox saved with one stops working. Use a separate Gmail account for receipts instead. If the page says app passwords are not available, the account is a Workspace account, is in Advanced Protection, or uses security keys only. Those accounts connect with Google instead (see below) or, for Workspace, ask the administrator for the Internal path.

Go to Settings > Email Receipts . In the manual form, fill in: Field Value IMAP server imap.gmail.com Port 993 Connection security TLS (usually port 993) User name the full Gmail address Password the 16-character app password Folder INBOX , or the label you dedicated to receipts (a nested label is Parent/Child ) Click Test connection . Monize logs in and reports "The connection works. The folder holds N messages." or the error the server returned. Click Save mailbox . Once saved, the password is never shown again. Editing the mailbox with the password left blank keeps the stored one.

With this path the user never types a password into Monize: they sign in at Google, approve the access, and Monize stores a refresh token (encrypted with ENCRYPTION_KEY ) that it trades for a short-lived access token every time it reads the mailbox. The IMAP host is always Google's own imap.gmail.com:993 ; the user does not choose a host or port. The Connect with Google button appears only after the administrator has registered an OAuth client and set both of its environment variables. One client serves every user of the deployment.

Decide the audience first, using the table above: Internal if your deployment belongs to a Google Workspace organisation and everyone who will connect is in it; otherwise External , which stays in Testing with its 7-day expiry. Sign in to the Google Cloud console and create a project (or pick one). No billing account is needed, and no API has to be enabled: IMAP sign-in uses only the OAuth scope. Open Google Auth Platform (the former "OAuth consent screen"; search for it in the console). Branding : give the app a name such as Monize and a support email. Add your deployment's domain under Authorized domains if the console asks for one. Audience : choose Internal or External . For External, add every Google account that will connect under Test users (up to 100). Leave the publishing status on Testing . Data Access : click Add or remove scopes and add https://mail.google.com/ (it is listed under Gmail API or can be pasted manually), plus openid and .../auth/userinfo.email . Save. Open Clients > Create client . Application type Web application , any name, and under Authorized redirect URIs add exactly: https://your-monize-host/settings/email-receipts/oauth-callback That is PUBLIC_APP_URL (no trailing slash) followed by /settings/email-receipts/oauth-callback . It must match character for character. Copy the Client ID and Client secret into the backend environment: PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://your-monize-host ENCRYPTION_KEY=... # already required for other secrets EMAIL_RECEIPTS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=1234567890-abc.apps.googleusercontent.com EMAIL_RECEIPTS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=GOCSPX-... Restart the backend. Settings > Email Receipts now shows Connect with Google above the manual form. A provider with only one of the two variables set is not offered at all. What Monize sends and stores: the authorization request asks for https://mail.google.com/ openid email with access_type=offline and prompt=consent , so Google returns a refresh token on every connection. The login name is the email address from the ID token. The refresh token is the only credential kept, encrypted; the access token lives in memory for one poll.

Go to Settings > Email Receipts and click Connect with Google . Choose the Google account. On an External client in Testing, Google warns "Google hasn't verified this app" : click Continue (this is expected; the administrator's project is unverified by design). An account that is not on the test-user list is refused here. Approve the access Google lists. The browser returns to Monize's Connecting the mailbox page, then to the settings with Connected to Google as you@gmail.com . Set the Folder to read ( INBOX or your receipts label), turn on Read the mailbox automatically , choose the AI mode , and click Save settings . See Mailbox Settings . Click Poll now to read the folder straight away and follow View the saved emails .

Reconnect runs the Google sign-in again and replaces the stored token. Use it when the panel says "The connection to Google is not active, so the mailbox is not being read. Connect again to resume." -- on an External/Testing client that happens every 7 days. Disconnect deletes Monize's stored token and stops reading the mailbox. Emails already stored are kept. Disconnecting does not withdraw the permission you granted. To do that, remove Monize on Google account permissions ; the panel links there. Revoking at Google without disconnecting in Monize is fine too: the next poll records "The mailbox's sign-in was revoked or has expired" and stops until you reconnect.

Microsoft 365 works the same way as Google: the administrator registers one app, and users click Connect with Microsoft . In the Microsoft Entra admin center , open App registrations > New registration . Platform Web , redirect URI ${PUBLIC_APP_URL}/settings/email-receipts/oauth-callback . Under Certificates & secrets , create a client secret and copy its value. Under API permissions , add the delegated permission IMAP.AccessAsUser.All (Office 365 Exchange Online) plus the OpenID permissions openid , email and offline_access . An organisation may still need to enable IMAP for the mailbox and allow users to consent to the app. Set the environment: EMAIL_RECEIPTS_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID=... EMAIL_RECEIPTS_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET=... EMAIL_RECEIPTS_MICROSOFT_TENANT=common # optional, default shown EMAIL_RECEIPTS_MICROSOFT_TENANT decides who may sign in: common (work, school and personal accounts), organizations , consumers , or one tenant's GUID or domain. A value that is not a valid tenant disables Microsoft sign-in and logs a warning. The IMAP host is fixed to outlook.office365.com:993 .

The manual form takes any IMAP server: host, port, TLS (usually 993) or STARTTLS (usually 143), user name and password. Most providers require an app password rather than the account password. The server's certificate is always verified; there is no "accept any certificate" switch. Two server-side rules apply to the host: Private addresses. A host that is a private, loopback or link-local address ( localhost , 192.168.x.x , a container name, .local , .internal ) can be used only by an administrator , unless the operator lists it in EMAIL_RECEIPTS_PRIVATE_HOST_ALLOWLIST (for example mail.lan:993,192.168.1.30:993 ). The check runs when the mailbox is saved and again on every connection. How much one poll reads. EMAIL_RECEIPTS_MAX_MESSAGES_PER_POLL (default 50) caps the messages read per poll; the rest wait for the next one. EMAIL_RECEIPTS_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES (default 2,000,000) is the largest message downloaded; a larger one is recorded as skipped and never fetched.

These settings are the same for a password mailbox and a connected one. Setting What it does Folder The folder to read. It is opened read-only. Changing it starts reading the new folder from the beginning. Read the mailbox automatically When on, Monize reads the mailbox every 15 minutes. Turning it off does not disconnect the mailbox, and Poll now reads it whether this is on or off. AI mode Off : the poll never calls the AI for receipts. On demand : the poll never calls the AI, but you can ask the assistant yourself from an email. Automatic : the poll asks the AI about a matched receipt that no approved profile could read completely, and drafts a profile for a sender that has none. Every AI answer is a proposal you approve. Apply proposals automatically Off by default. A proposal is applied without asking only when an approved profile read the whole email, the transaction was found by an order number or reference, or by exact amount and payee with a single candidate, and the proposal adds up to the cent. Everything else waits for your approval. Count profile proposals toward the daily AI limit On by default. Turn it off when a large batch of stored emails would otherwise use up the daily limit of AI-proposed changes. The status block shows the Last poll , the Last successful poll and the Last error , and offers Poll now and Delete mailbox . Deleting the mailbox removes the settings and every stored email from Monize; the emails in the mailbox itself are not touched.
